source.title: Irish News, 5 June 1964, p. 1 ("Rural council election results")
source.publisher: Irish News (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: the Gulladuff count read in the Irish News of 5 June 1964.

note: Triennial election of Magherafelt Rural District Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. The only contest was for the Gulladuff division, between two Nationalists. Twenty-four unopposed members added from the nominations report (Mid-Ulster Mail, 23 May 1964, p. 1), which names each with the division. 'There was no nomination for the Electoral Division of Swatragh which was previously represented by Mr. J. Harkin'; whether the 1962 rules deemed him re-elected is not confirmed, so Swatragh is not recorded; in 1967 James Harkin is again 'the outgoing member' for Swatragh (Mid-Ulster Mail, 20 May 1967, p. 1) (round-2 gap-fill, 7 Nov 2026). Printed: 'The outgoing representative, Mr. J. P. Kearney, was re-elected with 242 votes to 99 for his opponent, Mr. Patrick A. Boyle. There were four spoiled votes. The electorate was 401 and the number of votes cast showed a poll of 86 per cent.'
